correctness.rationale: The normalized graph-state coefficient matrix yields a direct finite-field character-sum identity, proving a flat spectrum with p^rank(D) eigenvalues. Direct edge accounting gives the 2x2 cyclic-shift cut block; an explicit Schur complement reduces its odd-skip kernel to f(P). The module F_p[X]/(X^m-1) proves nullity equals gcd degree without squarefreeness assumptions. In the five-step family the two polynomial factorizations and the root multiplicity in X^m-1 prove the exact valuations. The standalone direct-edge rank and independent Euclidean gcd implementations agree in 1,740 finite cases for p=2,3,5,7; 5 direct coefficient-spectrum comparisons pass to 5.56e-17, and the k=5 formulas pass m=6..299. No infinite statement is based solely on finite testing.

value.rationale: Generalized Petersen graphs are an infinite natural family of sparse cubic networks with many physically motivated finite-size instances. The exact Schmidt spectrum of a structured balanced cut is compressed to a fixed-degree cyclotomic polynomial. It reveals characteristic-sensitive entanglement deficits, persistent qutrit deficiency for all odd skips, and distinct two-adic and three-adic staircase phenomena on the same five-step family. This structural all-parameter law is neither a single ad hoc finite count nor a mere restatement of a universal graph-state rank theorem; its applicability is expressly limited to the stated cut and pure states.
